newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister meets Serbian opposition leader.
newsitem.headline: French minister meets Serbian opposition leader.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette met one of Serbia's main opposition leaders on Monday and urged Belgrade to recognise the outcome of municipal elections.

"I have told the Belgrade authorities tirelessly that the time when one could cancel elections, and ignore the people's will is over in Europe," de Charette told reporters after the 40-minute meeting with Vesna Pesic.

"Since the beginning of this crisis, France has put pressure (on Belgrade) so that a peaceful and democratic outcome is found. The result of the municipal elections must be accepted. We want dialogue to restart," de Charette said.

Pesic, one of the leaders of the eight-week-old peaceful demonstrations for democracy, said she was "extremely pleased" with her visit. She plans a news conference on Tuesday after meeting opposition Socialist leader Lionel Jospin.

Asked whether France planned to break off trade relations with Belgrade as Washington threatened to do at the weekend, a spokesman for de Charette said Pesic had cautioned against any pressure that could weigh "on the Serbian people".
"Pesic criticised actions against the Serbian people because the Serbian nationalists manipulate such actions," the spokesman said. "We have to continue political and diplomatic pressure."

U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for Europe John Kornblum said on Saturday that Washington was considering a unilateral freeze on new trade deals and official relations to pressure Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic into acknowledging opposition success at local elections.

He told reporters that the major powers' Contact Group on former Yugoslavia had ruled out international sanctions against Serbia but individual countries were independently examining ways of applying pressure to Milosevic.

Students and the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition have held daily protests for almost two months to force the Belgrade government to reinstate the results of municipal elections held on November 17.
